# Project workflow

Use Beads for issue work. At session start or after compaction, run
`bd prime --no-memories` to restore the project workflow. Read the assigned issue
with `bd show <issue-id>` before implementing. Start it with
`bd update <issue-id> --status in_progress`.

Use the Beads skill in `.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md` for this workflow. Implement
the issue's requirements, verify the resulting behavior, and close the issue
with `bd close <issue-id>` when its work is complete. Consult command help when
syntax is unclear. Preserve earlier files and task history.

# Project memory

Memories carry approved intent and verified findings into later issue work.
Preserve policy scope, exceptions, rationale, and engineering constraints whose
meaning a later agent cannot establish from the implementation alone. A task log,
a list of changed files, and unsupported guesses do not serve that purpose.

## Before a policy-dependent change

Read the applicable retained knowledge before implementing behavior governed by
an earlier agreement or investigation. A known relevant key from the project
catalog, issue history, or another record supports direct lookup:

```text
bd recall '<key>'
```

Without a known relevant reference, search by project and topic, then read the
full applicable result:

```text
bd memories '<query>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Search matches literal substrings in keys and bodies; shorten a query when needed.
Confirm project, scope, version, and evidence before applying a record. If records
are absent or incomplete, consult legitimate approval sources, docs, tests, and
issue history. Resolve conflicts against those sources. Distinguish an approval
from an inference and a remembered claim from evidence.

## Before closing a knowledge-producing issue

Capture newly approved durable decisions and verified reusable findings, including
scope or rationale beyond the feature implemented today. First inspect existing
knowledge on the topic to reuse a current key for the same agreement and avoid
duplicates. Choose a descriptive project/topic key for new knowledge.

Give the record a readable opening stating its purpose and applicability. Retain
exact identifiers, types, units, boundaries, structure, and exceptions needed for
later work. Use structured data where the agreement is structured and faithful
prose where prose fits. Cite actual approval or investigation sources. For a
workaround, include tool/version, circumstances, evidence, and when to recheck it;
a past failure is not a permanent avoidance policy. Report only validation that
actually occurred.

```text
bd remember '<complete record>' --key '<key>'
bd recall '<key>'
```

Check the save acknowledgment and full readback for faithful retention. Readback
verifies storage, not whether the saved claim is true. Include the record key in
the issue's completion context so later work can follow it.

## Revision, history, and reproduction

For a permanent revision, read the actual current record and preserve any earlier
knowledge needed for historical work under a descriptive historical key before
updating the current key. Carry unaffected facts forward. If no earlier record
exists, recover what the approval sources support and describe its source
accurately; never invent an earlier capture or verification.

Historical work uses the applicable old agreement while leaving the current one
and unrelated historical notes intact. Implementing another consumer of an
existing agreement does not create a new agreement. Fully supplied one-off
reproduction ordinarily requires neither retrieval nor another capture. Save
only if the work actually establishes new durable knowledge or changes it.

These legacy keys identify mutable notes. Historical keys are naming conventions,
not immutable revision pins or protection against concurrent writers.

## Project reference catalog

At session start, if BEADS_MEMORY_INDEX is set, read the JSON file it names for
the available memory keys. This catalog is a reference index, not the contents
of those records. Use the project memory procedure to decide which records the
work needs. An unset variable means this project uses search without a catalog.

○ trial-s5u · Quote a monthly statement total   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-08 · Updated: 2026-09-08

DESCRIPTION

  Meridian Credits quotes loyalty credits for a subscription reseller. The    
  local Python CLI accepts one JSON object on stdin and emits exactly one JSON
  object on stdout; run python3 main.py. Preserve {"command":"ping"} ->       
  {"status":"ok","product":"Meridian Credits"} and the existing unknown-      
  command response. No network, clock, locale or third-party package is       
  needed. Malformed input is outside these issues.                            
                                                                              
  A charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, 
  and charge_cents. The three IDs are nonempty strings; line_id is unique     
  within a request. A subscription is identified by the pair (account_id,     
  subscription_id); the same subscription_id can occur under different        
  accounts, and a subscription can have several charge lines. service_on is a 
  valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD date from 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31.         
  charge_cents is a nonnegative integer in US cents. No line is excluded by   
  its service date. Each request is the complete charge set of one            
  independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set. Line    
  collections may be empty. Lexicographic ID order means Unicode code-point   
  order. JSON object key order is immaterial; do not add response keys beyond 
  those specified.                                                            
                                                                              
  Release "1.0" is the initial agreement. An omitted release selects the      
  current agreement; an explicit supported release selects that version.      
  Versions introduced in an issue remain supported afterward. Public suites   
  name a specific release and send explicit release values, so their          
  expectations remain applicable when the current agreement changes. Run a    
  supplied suite with python3 test_public.py --cases PATH.                    
                                                                              
  Add total for a complete monthly statement. Request:                        
  {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...]} with optional release "1.0". Return  
  exactly release, credit_cents, and amount_due_cents for the whole charge set
  under the approved release agreement. The total must reflect that           
  agreement's credit-cap scope across the supplied lines. It is not a         
  collection of independent single-line quote requests. Keep quote available. 
                                                                              
  An empty statement returns                                                  
  {"release":"1.0","credit_cents":0,"amount_due_cents":0}. A statement        
  containing only the line in the quote example returns {"release": "1.0",    
  "credit_cents": 1999, "amount_due_cents": 18000}.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Meridian Credits local JSON CLI."""
3	import json
4	import sys
5	
6	CURRENT_RELEASE = "1.0"
7	
8	CAP_CENTS_1_0 = 2400
9	CREDIT_DIVISOR_1_0 = 10
10	
11	
12	def assigned_credit_cents_1_0(lines):
13	    """Release 1.0: each line earns floor(10% of charge), assigned within a
14	    2400-cent cap shared per account_id, earliest service_on first then
15	    increasing line_id."""
16	    credits = {}
17	    remaining = {}
18	    ordered = sorted(lines, key=lambda line: (line["service_on"], line["line_id"]))
19	    for line in ordered:
20	        uncapped = line["charge_cents"] // CREDIT_DIVISOR_1_0
21	        cap_left = remaining.setdefault(line["account_id"], CAP_CENTS_1_0)
22	        credit = min(uncapped, cap_left)
23	        remaining[line["account_id"]] = cap_left - credit
24	        credits[line["line_id"]] = credit
25	    return credits
26	
27	
28	def quote_1_0(line):
29	    credit = assigned_credit_cents_1_0([line])[line["line_id"]]
30	    return {
31	        "release": "1.0",
32	        "line_id": line["line_id"],
33	        "credit_cents": credit,
34	        "amount_due_cents": line["charge_cents"] - credit,
35	    }
36	
37	
38	def handle(request):
39	    command = request.get("command")
40	    if command == "ping":
41	        return {"status": "ok", "product": "Meridian Credits"}
42	    if command == "quote":
43	        release = request.get("release", CURRENT_RELEASE)
44	        if release == "1.0":
45	            return quote_1_0(request["line"])
46	        return {"error": "unsupported_release"}
47	    return {"error": "unknown_command"}
48	
49	
50	if __name__ == "__main__":
51	    json.dump(handle(json.load(sys.stdin)), sys.stdout)
52	    sys.stdout.write("\n")
53

2	import argparse
3	import json
4	from pathlib import Path
5	import subprocess
6	import sys

9	def equal(left, right):
10	    if type(left) is not type(right):
11	        return False
12	    if isinstance(left, dict):
13	        return left.keys() == right.keys() and all(equal(left[k], right[k]) for k in left)
14	    if isinstance(left, list):
15	        return len(left) == len(right) and all(equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(left, right))
16	    return left == right
17	
18	
19	parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
20	parser.add_argument("--cases", required=True)
21	args = parser.parse_args()
22	failed = 0

24	    try:
25	        if "artifact_json_path" in case:
26	            got = json.loads(Path(case["artifact_json_path"]).read_text())

29	                                  capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, timeout=5)

Meridian Credits release 1.0 credit agreement (approved by Finance; source: issue trial-2eq, 2026-09-08). Scope: all quote commands of the Meridian Credits CLI at release "1.0"; release 1.0 remains supported after later releases are introduced. An omitted release selects the current agreement; an explicit supported release selects that version.

Rules: each charge line's uncapped credit is 10% of charge_cents, rounded down separately to integer cents. A 2400-cent credit cap is shared by all lines with the same account_id, across its subscriptions; distinct account_id groups have independent caps. Within each cap group, credit is assigned by priority: earliest service_on first; equal service dates use increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order). Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the group's remaining cap; later lines receive only the remaining credit or zero. Total credit = sum of assigned line credits. A line's amount due = charge_cents minus its assigned credit; total due = total charges minus total credit.

Data model: a charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on (valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD, 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31), charge_cents (nonnegative integer US cents). line_id is unique within a request; a subscription is the pair (account_id, subscription_id); a subscription may have several lines. Each request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set; line collections may be empty. Malformed input is out of scope across these issues.

Implementation: main.py assigned_credit_cents_1_0 implements the full per-account cap assignment (sorted by (service_on, line_id)); quote_1_0 applies it to a single line, responding with exactly release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents (release always reported "1.0"). Verified: public_tests/release_1_quote.json via test_public.py PASS, plus tests/test_quote.py (example, omitted release, round-down, 2400 cap, zero charge, exact response keys). Multi-line assignment follows the same agreed algorithm but only single-line quoting is exercised by tests so far.

Close one or more issues.

If no issue ID is provided, closes the last touched issue (from most recent
create, update, show, or close operation). This fallback only applies in
interactive sessions (stdin is a terminal); in scripts and agent sessions a
missing ID is an error, so a command built from an empty variable cannot
silently close an unrelated issue. Set BD_LAST_TOUCHED_FALLBACK=1 to allow
the fallback anywhere, or =0 to disable it entirely.

When closing multiple issues, provide one --reason for all IDs or repeat
--reason once per ID. Reasons map positionally: the first --reason applies
to the first ID, the second --reason to the second ID, regardless of where
the flags appear in the command line.

Usage:
  bd close [id...] [flags]

Aliases:
  close, done

Flags:
      --claim-next           Automatically claim the next highest priority available issue
      --continue             Auto-advance to next step in molecule
  -f, --force                Force close pinned issues or unsatisfied gates

Scope: all quoting commands of the Meridian Credits CLI at release "1.0" — quote (single line) and total (whole monthly statement, added by issue trial-s5u under the same agreement); release 1.0 remains supported after later releases are introduced. A 2400-cent credit cap is shared by all lines with the same account_id, across its subscriptions; distinct account_id groups have independent caps. Within each cap group, credit is assigned by priority: earliest service_on first; equal service dates use increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order). Each line receives its uncapped credit up to the group's remaining cap; later lines receive only the remaining credit or zero. Total credit = sum of assigned line credits. A line's amount due = charge_cents minus its assigned credit; total due = total charges minus total credit. A total request is one cap-scoped quote of the complete supplied line set, not a collection of independent single-line quotes.

Data model: a charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on (valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD, 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31), charge_cents (nonnegative integer US cents). line_id is unique within a request; a subscription is the pair (account_id, subscription_id); a subscription may have several lines. Each request is the complete charge set of one independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set; line collections may be empty. Malformed input is out of scope across these issues.
